title: CENTCOM confirms hits Iranian air defence and naval sites after Hormuz mine attempt
body: Crude has been grinding higher through the week on the back of this escalation, with prices pushing toward their highest level in more than a month as the market prices in a prolonged disruption to exports rather than a quick de-escalation. Traders are increasingly focused on the mechanics of the standoff itself, including the scale of the US naval blockade around Iranian ports and the risk of further mining attempts in the Strait, rather than any single headline. With the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve already near multi-decade lows and no clear diplomatic off-ramp in sight, the geopolitical premium embedded in oil prices looks unlikely to unwind quickly. Attention now turns to whether Iran responds with further strikes on US assets or shipping, and to the upcoming OPEC+ meeting for any signal on supply policy. --- Earlier: investingLive Americas FX news wrap 1 Sept: It's a wrap but not for the Iran War. title: Dip buyers coming in: Schroders turns more bullish on gold citing central bank buying
body: Schroders' gold upgrade adds to a growing list of asset managers pointing to central bank demand as the structural underpin for prices, even after this year's sharp rally, suggesting institutional flows rather than retail momentum are driving the medium term case. The firm's decision to pair that with continued equity and technology exposure signals confidence that the current cycle has further to run, though its own acknowledgment that valuations sit in extended territory points to a market increasingly reliant on growth and earnings delivering without disappointment. The tactical tilt toward US Treasuries on attractive real yields suggests Schroders sees limited near term inflation risk, a view that would come under pressure quickly if price data surprises to the upside. Watch AI related earnings and inflation prints as the key swing factors for how long this constructive stance holds. --- Earlier: TD Securities sees gold risk to 4200 near term, 5350 target by 2027 --- Schroders is betting the cycle still has room to run, with gold now added as ballast against the risks it admits are building.

title: UBS's rate cut thesis meets a tougher test after Tuesday's yield surge
body: UBS's call rests on a widening gap between the front and back end of the curve, with long yields pricing in structural fiscal and issuance risk while short yields still have room to fall as disinflation takes hold. That divergence looks harder to defend after Tuesday, when yields across the curve pushed back toward levels last seen before the Treasury's buyback program expansion, suggesting markets are leaning toward pricing further hikes rather than the cuts UBS needs for its short duration thesis to pay off. Oil remains the key swing factor, with Brent above 92 dollars a barrel and no resolution in sight for Strait of Hormuz disruptions. Until inflation data confirms the fading contribution from energy and tariffs that UBS is banking on, the bank's preference for quality bonds at the front end carries more risk than the note lets on. --- An ugly Tuesday: investingLive Americas FX news wrap 1 Sept: It's a wrap but not for the Iran War. title: South Korea's August Inflation Edges Up to 3.1% Year-on-Year, Topping July's 2.8%
body: South Korea's consumer price inflation accelerated in August 2026, with the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rising 3.1% year-on-year, up from 2.8% in July 2026. The latest data, updated on 1 September 2026, show that price pressures have strengthened compared with the previous month on a year-over-year basis. The figures mean that both July and August readings are measured against the same months a year earlier, underscoring a clear pickup in annual inflation momentum heading into late summer. While July's 2.8% gain already signaled persistent price growth, August's 3.1% outcome highlights that inflationary forces have not yet fully eased in Asia's fourth-largest economy. The year-over-year comparison framework indicates that August's increase reflects faster price growth than in August of the prior year, while July's reading did the same against its year-earlier base. The move from 2.8% to 3.1% will likely refocus market attention on the future path of inflation and its potential implications for South Korea's broader economic outlook. title: NZX 50 Muted Ahead of RBNZ Rate Decision
body: New Zealand shares were little changed on Wednesday morning, with the benchmark index hovering around 13,789. This followed losses in the previous session and left the market at its lowest level since August 17, a trough first hit on Tuesday, as investors awaited the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's monetary policy decision later in the day. Markets widely expect the RBNZ to deliver a 25-basis-point rate hike, extending its tightening cycle after the increase in May. Sentiment was also subdued as higher oil prices stoked inflation concerns and reinforced expectations of further policy tightening amid escalating tensions in the Middle East. Sector performance was mixed: gains in communication services, industrials, and financials helped offset weakness in technology, consumer staples, and consumer discretionary stocks. On the macroeconomic front, New Zealand building permits fell 4.3% month-on-month in July, following a 3.7% decline in June, underscoring ongoing softness in construction activity. Among individual movers, Bankers Investment advanced 1.5% and Ebos Group added 0.9%, while A2 Milk and Fletcher Building slipped 0.7% and 0.5%, respectively. body: New Zealand's construction sector showed further signs of strain in July 2026, as building consents fell 4.3% month-over-month, deepening the decline from June's 3.7% drop. For investors and policymakers, the persistent softening in building consents may point to reduced pipeline activity in residential and commercial construction in the coming months. With approvals now falling at a faster rate, the data will likely feed into broader assessments of New Zealand's growth outlook and the health of its property and construction markets. title: US Crude Oil Inventories Resume Drawdown
body: US crude oil inventories declined by 2.6 million barrels in the week ending August 28, according to the American Petroleum Institute (API), partially offsetting a 4.2 million-barrel build in the previous week. Over the past 20 weeks, commercial crude stocks excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) have fallen by just over 48 million barrels, although total US crude inventories remain 3.1 million barrels higher year-to-date. The SPR saw a further draw of 3.1 million barrels, bringing total reserves down to 286.6 million barrels, a level that remains within the broadly accepted operational range of 250–300 million barrels. US crude production edged up to 13.843 million barrels per day (bpd) in the week ending August 21, from 13.830 million bpd a week earlier, representing a year-on-year increase of 461,000 bpd. On the products side, gasoline inventories rose by 300,000 barrels following a 3.2 million-barrel draw the previous week. Distillate stocks fell by 300,000 barrels, extending the prior week's 500,000-barrel decline. At the Cushing, Oklahoma, delivery hub, inventories increased by 200,000 barrels after a 1 million-barrel build in the preceding week.
